issues.title: Nonce never reaches the Next.js renderer, so the strict CSP blocks the app's own scripts
issues.description: The CSP header is set only on the *response*; Next.js extracts the nonce for its inline bootstrap/hydration scripts from the *request's* `Content-Security-Policy` header (the official pattern sets it on the forwarded `requestHeaders` as well, alongside `x-nonce`). As written, Next's inline scripts ship un-nonced, and under `script-src 'nonce-…' 'strict-dynamic'` (no `'unsafe-inline'` fallback) every page fails to hydrate — the CSP effectively breaks the entire app rather than protecting it. Fix: `requestHeaders.set("Content-Security-Policy", buildCsp(nonce))` before `NextResponse.next(...)`.

issues.title: Missing `worker-src` blocks the pdf.js worker, breaking/degrading PDF upload
issues.description: With `'strict-dynamic'` present, host sources like `'self'` are ignored, and workers can't carry nonces, so `worker-src` (falling back to `script-src`) blocks `new Worker(...)` for `pdf.worker.min.mjs` (`app/lib/utils/fileExtraction.ts:26-29`). At best pdf.js falls back to main-thread parsing (console errors, UI freezes on large PDFs); at worst PDF extraction — a core input path — fails outright. Add `worker-src 'self' blob:`.

issues.title: No dev-mode carve-out for `'unsafe-eval'` breaks `npm run dev`
issues.description: Next.js dev mode (React Refresh/HMR) requires `eval`, which this `script-src` forbids unconditionally. Once the P0 is fixed and the CSP actually takes effect, the dev server will throw CSP violations on every page; the standard pattern is to append `'unsafe-eval'` (or relax the policy) when `process.env.NODE_ENV === "development"`.

issues.title: Comment documents an incorrect nonce mechanism
issues.description: The comment claims Next.js tags its bootstrap scripts "with the nonce from the response's CSP header" — it actually reads the request header (this misunderstanding is the root cause of the P0). Left as-is, it will mislead future maintainers into thinking the response-only wiring is sufficient.

issues.title: Missing `form-action 'self'` directive
issues.description: The policy hardens `base-uri`, `object-src`, and `frame-ancestors` but omits `form-action`, leaving injected `<form action="https://evil…">` exfiltration unrestricted. Cheap to add alongside the existing hardening directives.

issues.title: No tests for the new CSP proxy
issues.description: The repo's guidelines call for tests alongside implementation; `buildCsp` and the nonce/header wiring are pure and easily unit-testable (e.g., asserting the CSP lands on both request and response headers), which would have caught the P0.
